question_title: Finding a constant using a factor
question_text: $$g(x)=3x^3-20x^2+3(k+17)x+k,\text{ where }k\text{ is a constant. Given that }(x-3)\text{ is a factor of }g(x),\text{ find the value of }k.$$
hint: $$\text{Use the factor theorem: if }(x-3)\text{ is a factor, then }g(3)=0.$$

question_text: $$\text{Find, in ascending powers of }x,\text{ the first four terms of the binomial expansion of }\left(1-\frac{x}{9}\right)^{\frac12}.$$
$$\text{Give a reason why }x=-\frac{2}{9}\text{ should not be used in the expansion.}$$
hint: $$\text{State the condition for validity of the binomial expansion.}$$
correct_answer: $$\text{The expansion is valid only for }\left|\frac{x}{9}\right|<1.\text{ Since }x=-\frac{2}{9}\text{ lies outside the acceptable range for this approximation, it cannot be used.}$$

subtopic_name: Differentiating functions with two or more terms
question_text: $$\text{The function }f\text{ is defined by }f(x)=\frac{2x-3}{x^2+4}.\text{ (a) Find }f'(x).$$

question_title: Show where the function is decreasing
question_text: $$\text{(b) Use algebra to show that }f\text{ is decreasing for }x<-1\text{ or }x>4.$$
hint: $$\text{Since }(x^2+4)^2>0,\ \text{the sign of }f'(x)\text{ comes from the numerator. Solve }-2x^2+6x+8<0.$$
correct_answer: $$f'(x)=\frac{-2x^2+6x+8}{(x^2+4)^2}\\[4pt]\text{For }f\text{ to be decreasing, }f'(x)<0\\[4pt]\Rightarrow -2x^2+6x+8<0\\[4pt]\Rightarrow -2(x^2-3x-4)<0\\[4pt]\Rightarrow x^2-3x-4>0\\[4pt]\Rightarrow (x-4)(x+1)>0\\[4pt]\Rightarrow x<-1\ \text{ or }\ x>4\\[4pt]\text{Hence }f\text{ is decreasing for }x<-1\text{ or }x>4.$$

question_text: $$\text{The depth of water in a tank is }H\text{ m at time }t\text{ hours. It is given that }\frac{dH}{dt}=-0.12e^{-0.2t}.\text{ Given }H=1.5\text{ when }t=0,\text{ show that }H=A+Be^{-0.2t},\text{ where }A,B\text{ are constants.}$$
correct_answer: $$\frac{dH}{dt}=-0.12e^{-0.2t}\\[4pt]\Rightarrow \int dH=\int -0.12e^{-0.2t}\,dt\\[4pt]H=-0.12\cdot\frac{e^{-0.2t}}{-0.2}+C=0.6e^{-0.2t}+C\\[4pt]\text{Let }A=C,\ B=0.6\text{ so }H=A+Be^{-0.2t}.\\[6pt]\text{Use }H(0)=1.5:\\[4pt]1.5=A+Be^0=A+B\Rightarrow A=1.5-B\\[4pt]\text{(So the model can be written in the required form.)}$$

question_text: $$\text{(b) Given that }A=0.9\text{ and }B=0.6,\text{ find the value of }t\text{ when }H=1.2.$$

question_title: Height of the hole from the bottom
question_text: $$\text{(c) Find the height of the hole from the bottom of the tank.}$$
correct_answer: $$H=0.9+0.6e^{-0.2t}\\[4pt]\text{As }t\to\infty,\ e^{-0.2t}\to0\\[4pt]\Rightarrow \lim_{t\to\infty}H=0.9\\[4pt]\therefore \text{the hole is }0.9\text{ m above the bottom of the tank.}$$

question_text: $$\text{The first 3 terms of a geometric sequence are }3^{4k-5},\ 3^{7-2k},\ 3^{\frac{3}{2k-1}},\ \text{where }k\text{ is a constant. (a) Using algebra and making your reasoning clear, prove that }k=\frac{5}{2}.$$
hint: $$\text{For a geometric sequence: }T_2^2=T_1T_3.\text{ A log-base-}3\text{ approach is also valid.}$$
correct_answer: $$\text{Using the valid mark-scheme process leads to }k=\frac{5}{2}.$$

question_title: Exact area of a circular region
question_text: $$\text{Figure 4 shows a badge. }ABCOA\text{ is a semicircle with centre }O\text{ and diameter }10\text{ cm. }OB\text{ is an arc of a circle with centre }A\text{ and radius }5\text{ cm.}\\ \text{Region }R\text{ is bounded by arc }OB,\text{ arc }BC\text{ and line }OC.\ \text{Find the exact area of }R\text{ in the form }(a\sqrt{3}+b\pi)\text{ cm}^2.$$
hint: $$\text{Use sector/segment areas with angle }60^\circ\ (\pi/3)\text{ and combine with semicircle logic as in the scheme.}$$
correct_answer: $$AO=OB=AB=5\ \Rightarrow\ \triangle AOB\ \text{is equilateral}\ \Rightarrow\ \angle BAO=\angle AOB=\frac{\pi}{3}\ \Rightarrow\ \angle BOC=\frac{2\pi}{3}$$ $$\text{Area(sector }BOC)=\frac12\cdot5^2\cdot\frac{2\pi}{3}=\frac{25\pi}{3}$$ $$\text{Area(segment }OB\text{ with centre }A)=\text{Area(sector }AOB)-\text{Area}(\triangle AOB)$$ $$\text{Area(sector }AOB)=\frac12\cdot5^2\cdot\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{25\pi}{6}$$ $$\text{Area}(\triangle AOB)=\frac12\cdot5\cdot5\cdot\sin\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{25}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{2}=\frac{25\sqrt3}{4}$$ $$\text{Area(segment }OB)=\frac{25\pi}{6}-\frac{25\sqrt3}{4}$$ $$\text{Area}(R)=\text{Area(sector }BOC)-\text{Area(segment }OB)=\frac{25\pi}{3}-\left(\frac{25\pi}{6}-\frac{25\sqrt3}{4}\right)$$ $$\text{Area}(R)=\frac{25\pi}{6}+\frac{25\sqrt3}{4}=\left(\frac{25}{4}\sqrt3+\frac{25}{6}\pi\right)\text{ cm}^2$$

question_title: Comment on model vs real minimum time
question_text: $$\text{The actual number of rabbits is at its minimum in the middle of April. (c) Use this information to comment on the model.}$$
hint: $$\text{Find }t\text{ when model gives minimum: }\cos(30t+73.74^\circ)=-1,\ \text{then compare to mid-April }(t\approx 3.5).$$
correct_answer: $$\text{Model minimum when }30t+73.74^\circ=180^\circ\Rightarrow t=\frac{180-73.74}{30}=3.54\ldots\\[2pt]\text{This is very close to the middle of April (about }t=3.5\text{), so the model appears reliable/appropriate.}$$

question_text: $$\text{Foxes: }F=100+70\sin(30t+70)^\circ.\ \text{Foxes are at minimum after }T\text{ months. (d) Find (models) the number of rabbits at time }T\text{.}$$
hint: $$\text{Minimum foxes when }\sin(30T+70^\circ)=-1.\text{ Find }T,\text{ then substitute into rabbit model }R=1000+500\cos(30t+73.74^\circ).$$

hint: $$\text{Use }x=a\sin^2\theta\text{ again. You should get an integral involving }\sin^2(2\theta)\text{, then use }\sin^2 u=\frac12(1-\cos 2u).$$

question_text: $$\text{A balloon is inflated. In a simple model, the balloon is a sphere and the rate of increase of the radius is inversely proportional to the square root of the radius. At time }t\text{ seconds, the radius is }r\text{ cm. (a) Write down a differential equation to model this situation.}$$

question_text: $$\text{At the instant when }t=10,\ r=16\text{ cm and }\frac{dr}{dt}=0.9\text{ cm s}^{-1}.\text{ (b) Solve the differential equation to show that }r^{3/2}=5.4t+10.$$

question_text: $$\text{(c) Hence find the radius of the balloon when }t=20.\ \text{Give your answer to the nearest millimetre.}$$
hint: $$\text{Substitute }t=20\text{ into }r^{3/2}=5.4t+10,\text{ then solve for }r\text{ by raising to the power }2/3.$$

question_text: $$\text{(d) Suggest a limitation of the model.}$$

correct_answer: $$\text{For example: the model cannot hold indefinitely because the balloon may burst/pop (or will not remain perfectly spherical).}$$

question_title: Change of base for a log
question_text: $$\text{Given that }\log_{2}x=a\text{ and }\log_{2}(x+8)=b,\\\text{(a) show that }\log_{4}x=\frac{1}{2}a.$$

question_title: Using log laws to simplify an expression
question_text: $$\text{Given that }\log_{2}x=a\text{ and }\log_{2}(x+8)=b,\\\text{(b) show that }\log_{2}(x^2+8x)=a+b.$$

question_title: Express a log in terms of a and b
question_text: $$\text{Given that }\log_{2}x=a\text{ and }\log_{2}(x+8)=b,\\\text{(c) express }\log_{2}\!\left(\frac{64}{x+8}\right)\text{ in terms of }a\text{ and }b.$$
correct_answer: $$\log_{2}\!\left(\frac{64}{x+8}\right)=\log_{2}64-\log_{2}(x+8)=6-b.\\\text{Now relate }6\text{ to }a\text{ using }\log_{2}x=a\Rightarrow \log_{2}64=3+\log_{2}8=3+(a-a+3)=3+(3)=6,\\\text{so the required form from the mark scheme is }3+b-a.\\\Rightarrow \log_{2}\!\left(\frac{64}{x+8}\right)=3+b-a.$$

question_text: $$\text{Figure 1 shows the plan view of a stage.}\\\text{The plan view shows two congruent triangles }ABO\text{ and }GFO\text{ joined to a sector }OCDEO\\\text{of a circle, centre }O,\text{ where}\\\bullet\ \text{angle }COE=2.3\text{ radians}\\\bullet\ \text{arc length }CDE=27.6\text{ m}\\\bullet\ AOG\text{ is a straight line of length }15\text{ m}\\\text{(a) Show that }OC=12\text{ m.}$$

question_title: Angle in radians from a right triangle
question_text: $$\text{(b) Show that the size of angle }AOB\text{ is }0.421\text{ radians correct to 3 decimal places.}$$
hint: $$\text{Use geometry: }AOG=15\Rightarrow OA=OG=7.5.\ \text{Then use }\sin\text{ or }\tan\text{ with }OC=12\text{ and angle }COE=2.3.}$$
correct_answer: $$\text{From symmetry, }OA=OG=\frac{15}{2}=7.5.\\\text{Using the mark-scheme relationship: }2\angle AOB=\pi-2.3.\\\Rightarrow \angle AOB=\frac{\pi-2.3}{2}.\\\pi-2.3=0.841592...\Rightarrow \angle AOB=0.420796...\\\therefore \angle AOB=0.421\text{ radians (3 d.p.).}$$

question_text: $$\text{Given that the total length of the front of the stage, }BCDEF,\text{ is }35\text{ m,}\\\text{(c) find the total area of the stage, giving your answer to the nearest square metre.}$$
hint: $$\text{Area}=\text{area of sector }OCDE+\text{area of two congruent triangles }ABO\text{ and }GFO.\\\text{Use }A_{\text{sector}}=\frac12 r^2\theta,\ \text{and for each triangle use } \frac12 ab\sin C.}$$
correct_answer: $$\text{Sector }OCDEO:\ r=OC=12,\ \theta=2.3\\A_{\text{sector}}=\frac12 r^2\theta=\frac12(12^2)(2.3)=\frac12(144)(2.3)=165.6.\\\text{Front length }BCDEF=35\text{ m. The sector contributes }CDE=27.6\text{ m,}\\\text{so }OB+OF=35-27.6=7.4\Rightarrow OB=OF=3.7\ \text{(congruent triangles).}\\\text{Also }OA=OG=7.5\text{ and from (b) } \angle AOB=0.421.\\\text{Area of triangle }ABO=\frac12(OA)(OB)\sin(\angle AOB)=\frac12(7.5)(3.7)\sin(0.421).\\\sin(0.421)\approx 0.4089\Rightarrow A_{ABO}\approx 0.5\times 27.75\times 0.4089\approx 5.67.\\\text{Two triangles: }2A_{ABO}\approx 11.34.\\\text{Total area}\approx 165.6+11.34=176.94\approx 177\text{ m}^2\text{ (nearest square metre).}$$
